[[File:Søren Galatius Oberwolfach 2021.jpg|thumb|Galatius at [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]] in 2021]]
'''Søren Galatius''' (born 1 August 1976) is a [[Danes|Danish]] mathematician who works as a professor of mathematics at the [[Columbia University]].<ref name="cv">{{Cite web|url=https://sorengalatius.com/|title=Søren Galatius, Professor of Mathematics|date=31 July 2025}}</ref> He works in [[algebraic topology]], where one of his most important results concerns the [[Homology (mathematics)|homology]] of the [[automorphism]]s of [[free group]]s.<ref>{{citation
 | last =Tillmann | first =Ulrike | author-link=Ulrike Tillman 
 | doi =10.1090/S0273-0979-2011-01360-X
 | issue =1
 | journal =[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]]
 | mr =2869008
 | pages =73–90
 | series =New Series
 | title =Spaces of graphs and surfaces: on the work of Søren Galatius
 | volume =49
 | year =2012| doi-access =free
 }}.</ref> He is also known for his joint work with [[Oscar Randal-Williams]] on moduli spaces of manifolds, comprising several papers. 

== Life == 
Galatius was born in [[Randers]], Denmark. He earned his PhD from [[Aarhus University]] in 2004 under the supervision of [[Ib Madsen]].<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=117706}}</ref> He then joined the [[Stanford University]] faculty, first with a temporary position as a [[Gábor Szegő|Szegő]] Assistant Professor and then two years later with a tenure-track position, eventually becoming full professor in 2011. He relocated to the [[University of Copenhagen]] in 2016. Since July 2025, he works as a professor at the [[Columbia University]].<ref name="cv"/>

== Recognition == 
In 2010, Galatius won the Silver Medal of the [[Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters]].<ref name="cv"/>
In 2012, he became one of the inaugural [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 19 January 2015.</ref>
He was an invited speaker at the 2014 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], speaking about his joint work with [[Oscar Randal-Williams]].<ref name="cv"/><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW-T4Diqn_8 Moduli spaces of manifolds], Søren Galatius, ICM 2014, accessed 18 January 2015.</ref> In 2017, he won an ''Elite Research Prize'' from the Danish Government for his work.<ref> [https://www.math.ku.dk/english/about/news/elite-research-prize-galatius/ Galatius receives Elite Research Prize]</ref> In 2022 he was awarded the [[Clay Research Award]] jointly with Oscar Randal-Williams.<ref>[https://www.claymath.org/events/news/2022-clay-research-award Clay Research Award 2022]</ref>
